newsitem.title: USA: Fed's inflation vigil may prolong growth - Broaddus.
newsitem.headline: Fed's inflation vigil may prolong growth - Broaddus.

text.p: President of the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond, Alfred Broaddus, said the central bank's "inflation vigilance" may prolong the current U.S. economic expansion.

"If we do that, I think there is an excellent chance that this expansion can continue not only in 1997 but beyond that," Broaddus told the Carolinas and Virginias chapter of Robert Morris Associates, a banking organization, here.
"The time to resist inflation is precisely the time when there isn't very much of it," Broaddus added.
Broaddus said the economic scenario continues to look good and, in many ways, as good as it gets. "The general economic picture is really bright, almost as bright as it gets," Broaddus said.
Citing a consensus of professional forecasters, Broaddus said that fourth quarter 1996 and first quarter 1997 Gross Domestic Product (GDP) growth combined may be over 4.0 percent.

He added that strong consumer spending has been a factor contributing to current U.S. economic expansion. "Consumer spending has been especially strong in this period and that's definitely been a factor," Broaddus said.
The Richmond Fed chief also reiterated that the sees the risks in the U.S. economy skewed to the upside. "My own feeling is that the risk in the forecast is weighed on the upside," Broaddus said.
